drug_identity.off_label_note: Used to decrease keratomalacia induced by matrix metalloproteinases in response to corneal infections.

cyp_profile.pathway_evidence: Topical ophthalmic application; systemic absorption profile is not primarily detailed for ophthalmic route.

metabolism_and_clearance.extra_information: Following a single topical dose, tear film concentrations surpass MICs for common ocular pathogens.

organ_burden_logic.note: Topical ophthalmic use generally minimizes systemic organ burden, but cats have a specific hypersensitivity risk.

blood.evidence: Some cats may have an anaphylactic reaction to the polymyxin B component that necessitates discontinuation.

timing_profile.evidence: Acts locally on the epithelial membranes and other tissues of the eye.

_ddi_note: Oxytetracycline should not be mixed directly (in vitro) with any other drugs.

dosage_list.duration_note: Apply 2 to 4 times daily. Chlamydia spp infections should be treated for 3 to 4 weeks beyond resolution of clinical signs.

contraindications.condition: History of hypersensitivity to either drug or components

effects_and_mechanisms.common_mechanism: Tetracyclines reversibly bind to the 30S ribosomal subunits to disrupt protein synthesis. Polymyxin B interacts with the lipopolysaccharide of the cytoplasmic outer membrane of gram-negative bacteria, altering membrane permeability.
effects_and_mechanisms.dog_mechanism: Upregulates transforming growth factor-beta and inhibits matrix metalloproteinases (MMP-9, MMP-2) by binding calcium and zinc.

species_notes.dog: May accelerate corneal epithelial wound healing in dogs. Decreases keratomalacia induced by matrix metalloproteinases in infected corneal ulcers.
species_notes.cat: Frequently effective for treating Chlamydia spp and Mycoplasma spp conjunctivitis. Chlamydia infections require treatment 3-4 weeks beyond resolution. Some cats may experience severe anaphylactic reactions to Polymyxin B.

dog.evidence: Generally well tolerated by the epithelial membranes and other tissues of the eye.

cat.evidence: Some cats may have an anaphylactic reaction to the polymyxin B component that necessitates discontinuation of treatment.

storage_and_forms.storage: Store at controlled room temperature (20°C-25°C [68°F-77°F]), away from moisture and sunlight; do not freeze.

section_1_2_10.highlights: Used to treat superficial ocular bacterial infections. Frequently effective for Chlamydia and Mycoplasma in cats (treat 3-4 weeks past clinical signs). Risk of local irritation or anaphylaxis in cats.
section_1_2_10.indications: Prevent or treat superficial ocular infections involving the conjunctiva and/or cornea caused by gram-positive, gram-negative, and intracellular bacteria.
section_1_2_10.client_info: Use proper administration techniques to avoid contamination. Wait 5 minutes before applying other eye medications. Crystals may appear on the surface of the eye (not harmful).
